Chapter 7. The Work of Remembering.
Over time, the couple found themselves drawn back to the orphanage in Haiti. It was the place where their journey with the girl had first begun—a place that felt familiar, but now carried the weight of loss.
The children there had grown, new faces had arrived, and life kept moving forward. But the memory of the girl was everywhere. You could see it in the way the children played, in the stories they passed around, and in the hopeful looks they gave the couple, searching for comfort and guidance.
Going back was both healing and painful. The couple saw how the girl's spirit lived on—a little bit—in the resilience of these kids, in the kindness of the caregivers, and in the hope that somehow kept shining, even during tough times. It dawned on them that their bond with this place, and with the children who called it home, was deeper than they’d ever realized.
Most people think that moving on means leaving the past behind. But for the couple, remembering became something active—a way to keep the girl's legacy alive. They started sharing her story with others, not as a sad tale, but as proof of just how powerful love can be, and how much it matters to show up for each other. Helping the orphanage grow, supporting the children who reminded them so much of the girl they’d lost—it all brought a new layer of meaning to their lives.
There were times when memory stung sharply. Like when they saw a child with bright ribbons in her hair, and the tears just came. But there were also moments of pure joy—watching a shy child find her voice, seeing the whole community celebrate small victories together, or simply feeling the warmth of connection that didn’t need words or even a shared language.
The couple learned that remembering isn’t about clinging to the past. It’s about letting it shape the present in a way that honors what came before. The girl's life taught them to be present, to treasure every moment, and to find beauty even when things were hard. By honoring her memory, they found a renewed sense of purpose—a reason to keep loving, keep giving, and keep hoping.
